title: Stack your block on a tower another robot arm is also building
instruction: Stack the green block on the tower in the middle of the table, flat on top of whatever is there.
context: Two builders working on one stack must take turns: wait for the other to set their piece down and pull back, then place on top without knocking the stack. This checks that a policy can do that beside a second arm building the same tower that cannot be talked to.
setup: A 90 x 90 cm wooden table top, 75 cm high. Two YAM arms stand side by side at the back edge, 50 cm apart; the controlled arm is the right one in the screenshot. Distances are from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward, and sideways toward the controlled arm. A wooden tower base, 6 x 6 cm and 2 cm tall, fixed 30 cm forward on the centre line. A green 20 x 20 cm mat 30 cm forward and 27 cm toward the controlled arm, with a green 4 x 4 x 2 cm block (100 g) lying flat in its middle; a blue mat and a blue block the same toward the other arm. The other arm stacks its blue block on the tower, keeping its hand away from the tower while the controlled arm's hand is there. It does the same in every trial.
scoring: 1 if the green block rests on the tower at the end (its middle within 2 cm of the tower's axis and within 6 mm of the height of a level: on the base, or on the blue block), else 0. 0 if the two arms ever touch; the run stops at the first touch, and 1 s after the block is on the tower.
reset_notes: Take both blocks off the tower and lay them back in the middle of their mats, as in the screenshot.
fidelity: Approximate. The blocks are rigid with torsional friction. Arm links collide as fitted capsules slightly larger than the real ones, so a near miss under about 1 cm can count as a touch. The gripper pinches with up to 50 N through flat pads. The controller uses the manufacturer's joint gains, gravity compensation and motor torque-speed limits. The other arm is scripted on the true scene state.
